items.stem: Answer ANY ONE of the following two questions, in about 100–120 words : 6 I. Examine the similarities and differences between the tiger in “A Tiger in the Zoo” and the dragon in “The Tale of Custard the Dragon”.
items.answer: The tiger and Custard the dragon both represent strength, but their circumstances and behaviour contrast sharply. The tiger is confined in a zoo cage, which prevents him from living freely and expressing his natural power. He feels restless, angry, and helpless. On the other hand, Custard is considered cowardly and is often mocked by others. However, when danger appears in the form of a pirate, Custard bravely kills him and saves everyone. The tiger symbolizes trapped strength, while Custard represents hidden courage. Thus, while both are strong creatures, the tiger suffers from captivity, whereas Custard proves his bravery through action. items.stem: Are you concerned about traffic, and road safety? What are your concerns ? How would you make road travel safer and more enjoyable?
items.answer: About these three topics, we can discuss topic number 2. An Unforgettable Journey It is about a journey which will remain fresh till there are breaths left with me. The incident goes back to the year 2006 when all the members of my family were returning after worshipping the shrine of Vaishno Devi. We were accompanied by two other families from our neighbourhood. The Jammu Mail started well in time from Jammu. Every thing was in high spirits. All were happy to have a decent trip. In the way we enjoyed with songs tit- bits and other amusing material. It was 8.00 a.m. when the train passed Jalandhar. There we heard the rattling and roaring. In no time, the train stopped with a sudden and rapid jerk. Many passengers fell from their upper berths. There were wailings, cries and stampede every where. The passengers were jumping from the compartment to save themselves. All were in a very odd as well as tantalising situation. There was no alternative left with the people. We too got down from- the train and came in the open. On having a close look at the train, we saw eight bogies were derailed with their wheels in the concrete and the small pebbles. On further enquiry it was found that the track was damaged. Near about one full length of the rail measuring seven metres was not there. All left the place. Ambulance and police arrived in no time. The railway officials and the nearby villagers came running to help the passengers. It was a heart-rending scene. Small children along with their mothers were weeping bitterly. But God be thanked that there was no loss of life! A few passengers got slight injuries otherwise all were okay. Whenever I enjoy a long journey, I immediately think of journey by Jammu Mail.

items.answer: 2024 Valli was a young girl of 8 years who still displayed mature and responsible behaviour in the story. She was bold enough to fulfil her desire of riding a bus without her parents help in any way. I think Anne Frank had the same characteristics. Even after being punished thrice for talking in class, she did not get depressed and accepted the punishment intelligently. items.stem: You have been asked to give a speech on the topic ‘The journey is more important than the destination’. Prepare a draft for the speech, in not more than 120 words, with reference to the texts Madam Rides the Bus and The Black Aeroplane. You may begin this way: Good morning, everyone. Today, I would like to talk to you about how the journeys that we experience in life are often more important than their destinations. You may end this way : To conclude, I would like to say that... Thank you.
items.answer: 2023 Good morning, everyone. Today, I would like to talk to you about how the journeys that we experience in life are often more important than their destinations. In ‘Madam Rides the Bus’, Valli’s journey was initially filled with excitement. It was only when she saw the young cow dead on the road that her spirits dampened. This experience made her learn about life and death. Similarly, the pilot in ‘The Black Aeroplane’ was guided to safety by another plane when his plane went into a storm. However, he later learned that there were no other planes in the sky! Valli’s bus ride symbolises a journey of exploration and self-discovery, through the storm represents a journey of courage and resilience. To conclude, I would like to say that you should enjoy every moment of your journey, because that’s where you’ll find the true treasures. items.stem: Valli’s dream was to enjoy a ride on the bus to the nearest town. What preparations did she make to realize her dream?
items.answer: 2019 It is quite natural when we want to fulfil our desires; some temptations always come in our way. In the story, we see that Valli had the deepest desire to enjoy a ride on the bus. She usually stood in the front doorway of her house and carefully watched how a bus ran from her village to the nearby town every day. So, a temptation raised in her mind to ride on this bus. As her desire and temptation go together, so Valli was courageous and confident to fulfil her desire. She collected every desired piece of information about journey such as distance, fare and time of bus journey. So, she took a great risk to ride the bus. However, she slipped out of the house without her mother’s knowledge and managed to fulfil her desire of enjoying a bus ride.

items.stem: How did Valli save money for her first bus journey? Was it easy for her ? What does it show about her ? Or How did Valli plan herself to have a ride in the bus? Or How did Valli save money for her first bus journey? Or How did valli save up money for her first journey? What made her laugh on her way?
items.answer: 2016, 2014, 2010 Valli was overwhelmed with a tiny desire of having a bus ride. She had two problems namely fare-money and leaving the house without intimating her mother. In order to overcome both the problems, she planned everything very well. About the fare and the bus, she heard the conversation of daily commuters. Thus she had picked up various small details about the bus journey, fare, timings etc. About the fare, she saved all the stray coins that came in her hands. The next severe problem pertained when and how to leave the house. Ultimately she decided that the afternoon time was most suitable for that. At that time her mother had a short nap after lunch. So she decided to ride the afternoon bus and return by two-forty-five.

items.stem: What was Valli’s greatest desire? How did she fulfil it?
items.answer: 2012 Valli’s greatest desire was to ride on the bus that travelled between her village and the nearest town. The sight of the bus, filled each time with a new set of passengers, was a source of unending joy for Valli. Over many days and months, Valli listened conversations between her neighbours and the passengers who rode the bus. This way, she picked up various small details about the bus journey. Valli had the desired information about journey like how many miles away the town was, what the fare was and how much time it took to complete the bus journey. Then she started to save money. She did not buy toys, balloons, etc. Even she did not ride on the merry-go-round in the village fair. At last, on a fine spring afternoon, she rode on the bus and started her journey. Thus, Valli fulfilled her indomitable desire to ride the bus.

items.stem: What are the incidents and experiences that present Valli as a mature girl ahead of her age?
items.answer: 2005 Valli was an eight-year-old village girl. She had no playmates. Her favourite pastime was to stand at the doorstep and watch things and people. This way she not only satisfied her curiosity but also gained new experiences. Her strongest desire was to go for a bus-ride. She meticulously planned for it - gathered information about the distance, time and ticket money. Showing self-restraint, she resisted the temptation to buy peppermint, toys or a ride on the merry-go-round in order to save 60 paisa for the bus journey. She boarded the bus without anyone’s help, refused a free treat by the conductor and didn’t talk to strangers. This shows her commanding, confident and self-dependent nature. This also shows her determination and maturity at such a little age.
